question: Should tools.exec.denylist override ordinary full/off and durable trust while preserving authorized elevated-full as the sole explicit break-glass bypass?
rationale: This choice defines what operators may rely on as a STOP rule and whether the existing elevated-full contract remains stronger than the new policy; code review cannot choose that security promise without owner intent.

options.title: Approve the break-glass exception
options.body: Keep the current design, where ordinary full/off and durable trust stop for approval but an explicitly authorized elevated-full invocation bypasses the denylist.

options.title: Make STOP rules absolute
options.body: Require denylist matches to prompt even under elevated-full, with corresponding runtime, documentation, and regression updates.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Leave the canonical issue open until maintainers define a narrower or differently named policy contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the break-glass exception
recommendation.body: Keep the current design, where ordinary full/off and durable trust stop for approval but an explicitly authorized elevated-full invocation bypasses the denylist.

likelyOwner.reason: The current exec approval and system.run security model appears primarily shaped by this person's merged history.
